description: The pie chart depicts the distribution of stimulus types used by journalists when providing input to Large Language Models (LLMs) during WildChat conversations. The chart contains seven slices, representing different categories of stimulus material. The largest slice, labeled “Draft/Other,” is red and represents approximately 26.4% of the total. “Press Release” is the next largest, colored yellow and accounting for 18.7%. “External News Article” is blue and represents 18.1%, while “Interview” is dark purple and accounts for 8.8%. “Organizational Report” is colored navy and represents 7.7%, followed by “Event Posting” in purple at 6.6%. The remaining slices are “Intra-agency news article” (4.9%, teal), “Organizational Website” (4.9%, dark blue), and “Social Media Post” (1.1%, orange). The chart includes a legend labeling each slice with its corresponding color, and percentage labels are displayed directly within each slice. The slices appear to be ordered clockwise, generally from largest to smallest proportion.
caption_used: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of various input stimulus material types provided by journalists to LLMs during WildChat conversations, matched to online articles from two identified news agencies. The largest category is 'Draft/Other,' accounting for approximately 26.4% of the total, followed by 'Press Release' at 18.7%. 'External News Article' and 'Interview' are the next largest categories, representing 18.1% and 8.8%, respectively. Notably, 'Organizational Report' consistently exceeds 'Event Posting,' with 9.7% compared to 6.6%. Additionally, 'Social Media Post' shows a slight increase over 'Email,' with 1.5% versus 2.7%. The chart provides a clear overview of the relative proportions of each stimulus type, with all categories labeled and color-coded for clarity.
